title: SCHC profile ceiling off-by-one: C emits 22555-byte Rule255 datagram peers reject; 31-byte reject band vs peers
description: P2, found by kimi correctness and kimi edge-cases passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c:538-540 caps compress INPUT at SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (22554) but the ceiling is on the ENCODED datagram including the rule byte (per size_boundary vectors; Rust codec.rs:2258). Two divergences: (a) pkt_len == 22554 passes the > check and the fallback emit (lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c:125-131) writes 1 + 22554 = 22555 bytes - one over the ceiling; Rust decode_rule255 (codec.rs:1460) and Python decode_rule255 (headers.py:206) reject len > 22554, so C emits a datagram peers drop (silent TX blackhole at the boundary); (b) conversely well-formed compressible inputs in (22554, 22585] (rule-0 encoded size = pkt_len - 31) are accepted by Rust enforce_encoded_profile_limit (codec.rs:2181) and Python (headers.py:872-873) but rejected by C's input cap - fail-closed, local-only. Pre-existing (blame 660b9bf3bf), adjacent to the hahk gate. Fix: drop the input cap, enforce needed > SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE at the two Rule255 emit sites and per-rule encoded-size checks, mirroring Rust's structure; pin both boundary directions with size_boundary vectors and rerun the parity gate.
